title: 2005 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement: A wooden cube \(n\) units on a side is painted red on all six faces and then cut into \(n^3\) unit cubes. Exactly one-fourth of the total number of faces of the unit cubes are red. What is \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The \(n^3\) unit cubes have \(6n^3\) faces total. The red faces are exactly the surface of the original cube, \(6n^2\) of them.

Setting the red fraction to one-fourth, \[ \dfrac{6n^2}{6n^3} = \dfrac{1}{n} = \dfrac{1}{4}, \] so \(n = 4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count the total number of small-cube faces and the number that are red
